newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat sees steady growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indosat sees steady growth in 1997.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications company PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) said on Friday it was poised for steady growth this year on the back of a 490-billion rupiah ($207 million) expansion programme.

"We have allocated an investment fund of 490 billion rupiah (in 1997), so we hope the net profit growth in 1997 can reach 12 to 14 percent," Indosat president-director Tjahjono Soerjodibroto told a news conference.
He said the funds would be used to expand business in Indonesia as well as improving the company's regional and international telecommunication services.
Indosat, which is listed on both the Jakarta and the New York stock exchanges, posted a 1996 net profit growth of eight percent over 1995.
In the first nine months of 1996, Indosat reported a net income of 361.6 billion rupiah, compared with 342.9 billion rupiah in the same period of 1995.

Soerjodibroto said in a statement that Indosat planned to improve its services during 1997 by completing an optic fibre project connecting the capital Jakarta and the country's second largest city, Surabaya.
Other such projects to be completed through the year were services linking Jakarta and other cities in the Asia-Pacific region, Australia, the Middle East and Western Europe, he said.
Soerjodibroto said Indosat would also launch a satellite telephone service using the London-based International Maritime Satellite (Inmarsat). He did not give details.
He also said the government's reduction in international telephone rates from January 1 would have no impact on Indosat's revenues.
"There won't be any impact on Indosat's revenue. We will keep growing as usual," he said.

Soerjodibroto said a proposal by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to reduce Indonesia's current accounting rate to the United States to $1.30 minute from January 1 from $1.40 would also have a little effect.
"Even though the accounting rate is down, the effect on revenue will be little," he said.
Indosat projected its market share as an international telecommunications service provider in Indonesia at between 80 and 83 percent in the year 2000, compared to 91 percent currently.
